column1: # NVIDIA-only settings in fine-tuning code and configuration, read by
# checks/apple-silicon.sh. One rule per line: an extended regular expression
# (git grep -E), a tab, and the Apple Silicon alternative shown on a match.
# A matching line that ends with the comment "apple-silicon: allow" is
# accepted, for example a device fallback that also handles CUDA machines.

column2: .cuda() moves tensors to an NVIDIA GPU. Use .to(device) with device "mps" (PyTorch) or MLX, which uses the GPU by default.
torch.cuda is NVIDIA-only. Use torch.backends.mps.is_available() and torch.mps.
A "cuda" device string. Use "mps" for PyTorch on Apple Silicon.
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES selects NVIDIA GPUs. Apple Silicon has one GPU, which MPS and MLX use automatically.
cuDNN is NVIDIA-only. Remove cudnn settings.
NCCL is NVIDIA-only. Use the "gloo" distributed backend.
FlashAttention needs NVIDIA GPUs. Use attn_implementation="sdpa".
bitsandbytes quantization targets CUDA. Quantize with MLX (mlx_lm.convert -q, QLoRA in mlx_lm.lora) or train in bfloat16.
bitsandbytes optimizers target CUDA. Use optim="adamw_torch".
fp16 mixed precision in the transformers Trainer targets CUDA. Use bf16=True on Apple Silicon.
fp16 mixed precision in accelerate targets CUDA. Use bf16 or no.
Multi-GPU accelerate modes need NVIDIA GPUs. Use distributed_type: NO.
This library needs NVIDIA GPUs. Use mlx-lm for LoRA fine-tuning and serving, or PyTorch on MPS.
